## Custom Oxlint Rules

Custom rules are split by plugin namespace and configured in
`oxlint.config.ts`:

- `tools/oxlint/effect-rules.js` owns po…2764 tokens truncated…                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |

Globally enabled rules:

- `effect/no-switch`: use Effect `Match` with exhaustive handling instead of
  `switch`.
- `effect/no-manual-tag`: use `Data` or `Schema` tagged constructors instead of
  manual `_tag` object literals.
- `effect/no-error-tag-comparison`: use `Effect.catchTag`/`catchTags` for
  handling tagged errors, or `Match.value`/`Schema.is` for typed predicates,
  and `Option.isSome`/`isNone`/`match` for options instead of comparing
  `error._tag` or `cause._tag` directly. Test assertions and tags on values
  that are not named `error` or `cause` remain outside this syntax-only rule.
- `effect/no-conditional-object-spread`: schema-backed optional fields should be
  owned by schemas and handled with `Option`, not object-spread shaping.
- `site/no-context-nullish-default`: SEO/content metadata should come from
  canonical schemas rather than ad hoc `??` fallbacks.
- `effect/no-layer-exports-in-service-files`: service files own contracts;
  production/test layers belong in layer modules.
- `bun/no-node-runtime`: Bun is the script/runtime boundary for this repo;
  executable Effect entrypoints should use `BunRuntime`.
- `bun/no-node-runtime-import`: Bun-first runtime code must not import
  `NodeRuntime` modules. Use the Bun runtime module at executable boundaries.
- `bun/no-bun-file-outside-adapter`: keep `Bun.file`, `Bun.write`,
  `Bun.spawn`, and similar file/process host APIs in runtime, main, CLI,
  `*.layer.ts`, `bun.layer.ts`, `live.layer.ts`, or test files.
- `bun/no-direct-bun-host-access`: on the exact MCP promotion preflight test
  path, reject `Bun.which`, `Bun.spawn`, `Bun.spawnSync`, `Bun.file`, and
  `Bun.write`. That lifecycle test owns temporary files and Git processes
  through Effect Platform `FileSystem`, `Path`, and `ChildProcess` services;
  the rule deliberately does not widen this stricter policy to unrelated test
  or adapter boundaries. A transient exact-path fixture proves the direct Bun
  calls and raw Effect runtime execution remain rejected.
- `bun/no-bun-runtime-outside-entrypoint`: keep `BunRuntime.runMain` in
  executable entrypoints: `main`, `*.runtime`, CLI, or top-level `scripts/*`
  files. Service and package code should return Effect programs.
- `mdx/no-route-local-mdx-component-registry`: route files should import the
  shared app MDX component registry or package-owned MDX primitives instead of
  declaring `mdxComponents`, MDX-shaped `components` objects, or inline
  `<MDX components={{ ... }} />` registries.
- `site/no-unscoped-tanstack-server-functions`: TanStack
  `createServerFn`/`createServerOnlyFn` imports are banned except for the
  documented Markdown middleware `createServerOnlyFn` fence, which exists
  because production import protection rejects direct `runtime.server` imports
  through `src/start.ts`.
- `site/no-route-local-seo`: TanStack route files must use the generated
  `routeSeo`/`RouteSeoPage` pipeline instead of route-local `seo({ ... })`
  objects.
- `site/no-manual-json-ld-script`: TanStack route files must not hand-author
  `application/ld+json` scripts; JSON-LD is generated from
  `@packages/seo`.
- `site/no-module-owned-public-asset-url`: app JSX must import ordinary image
  and pattern assets from `$/assets`. The narrow rule rejects only `/images/*`
  and `/patterns/*` `src` literals; external URLs plus stable public PWA,
  CSS-token, and OG URLs remain explicit contracts. Oxlint 1.80 has no native
  `no-restricted-syntax` rule, so this fixture-backed `site/*` rule is the
  narrowest supported implementation.

Scoped Effect-owned code rules:

The global `site/no-relative-workspace-imports` rule resolves relative imports
and rejects any target owned by another app or package, including direct paths
into `apps/**` or `packages/**` and shortened sibling paths such as
`../../scripts/src/**`. Workspace consumers must use an explicit package or
app export. Because this rule is separate from narrower
`no-restricted-imports` policies, those policies cannot silently replace the
workspace boundary. Unit and executable lint fixtures prove root-to-workspace
and sibling-workspace rejection, same-workspace relative imports, and an
accepted `@packages/*` export.

The strict Effect-owned override covers `packages/aeo/src`,
`packages/effect-start/src`, `packages/http-api/src`, `packages/og/src`,
`packages/mcp/src`, `packages/posts/src`, `packages/rpc/src`, `packages/scripts/src`,
`packages/seo/src`, `apps/web/src/lib`, the Vite build adapters
`apps/web/vite.config.ts` and `apps/web/vite-og-assets.ts`, the root
deployment, state-read and destroy Alchemy entrypoints,
`packages/infrastructure/src/**/*.ts`, the root Axiom readback runtime, the
generated-asset runtime, and the MCP workerd boundary and runtime.

Host-framework adapters are exception-scoped instead of excluded wholesale.
Vite plugin callbacks, live Playwright/Lighthouse/command adapters, and final
CLI process boundaries may keep raw host signatures only in the explicitly
configured override files. Durable parsing, schema encoding, command policy,
route evidence, preview deploy policy, Lighthouse behavior, and build/deploy
policy still live behind Effect services, schemas, configs, and layers.

- `effect/no-typeof`, `effect/no-instanceof`, and `effect/no-in-operator`: decode
  unknown shapes with owning schemas and branch with `Match`, `Option`,
  `Result`, or `Exit`.
- `effect/no-undefined-comparison` and `effect/no-nullish-comparison`: model
  optionality with schemas and branch with `Option`.
- `effect/no-throw`: return typed tagged failures through Effect.
- `effect/no-async-await-promise`: compose Effect programs instead of mixing
  service code with raw promises. The rule covers async declarations,
  expressions, and arrows; `Effect.promise`, `Effect.tryPromise`, live adapter
  functions, and host-required framework callbacks are the allowed external
  Promise boundaries.
- `effect/no-bare-effect-try-promise`: imported or aliased `Effect.tryPromise`
  calls must use `{ try, catch }` so Promise rejection becomes the boundary's
  canonical tagged error. The rule ignores unrelated local `Effect` and
  `tryPromise` identifiers.
- `effect/no-defecting-web-crypto-digest`: imported or aliased
  `Effect.promise` callbacks may not contain `crypto.subtle.digest`, including
  block bodies, because that host Promise can reject. Use direct typed
  `Effect.tryPromise({ try, catch })`. The rule is intentionally syntax-specific
  and does not infer fallibility for arbitrary Promise APIs.
- `effect/no-unbranded-identifier-schema`: in the strict MCP source scope,
  identifier-shaped fields such as `uri`, `slug`, `cursor`, `operation`, and
  `uriTemplate` must use an owning branded or literal Schema. The rule follows
  local Schema aliases and `.make` builders so a plain string cannot evade the
  field check through a one-line alias. Raw invalid ingress diagnostics remain
  explicit and are not silently widened into domain identifiers.
- `effect/no-json-parse-stringify`: use schema encode/decode helpers at JSON
  boundaries.
- `effect/no-native-collections`: use `HashMap` and `HashSet` when keyed
  collection semantics matter.
- `effect/no-native-array-methods`: scoped narrowly to package/service code where
  Effect collection helpers are expected, including posts source policy.
- `effect/no-runtime-execution-outside-boundaries`: package/service code returns
  Effect values; runtime files and app loaders own execution.
- `effect/no-ambient-time-or-random`: deterministic Effect-owned code should
  receive time/randomness as explicit input or Effect services.
- `effect/no-nested-wrapper-calls`: prefer pipe-first transformations over nested
  wrapper composition. It also catches tiny `map*`, `to*`, `decode*`, and
  `encode*` helpers passed into Effect mapper calls, Schema encode/decode
  helpers, or RPC adapter mapping.
- `effect/no-process-boundary-outside-config`: keep `process.env` and
  `process.argv` reads in config, runtime, main, CLI, layer, or test
  boundaries.
- `effect/no-console-outside-runtime`: keep `console.*` in runtime, CLI,
  adapter, or test boundaries; services return typed values or tagged errors.
- `effect/no-schema-decoder-outside-ingress` and
  `effect/no-schema-encoder-outside-egress`: detect `Schema` and
  `SchemaParser` codec execution, while excluding `decodeTo` and `encodeTo`
  transformations. Decoder rules apply only at explicit ingress scopes;
  encoder rules apply only at serialization egress scopes.
- `effect/no-throwing-schema-sync-codec`: forbids throwing `*Sync` codecs in
  production scopes, including top-level constants. `effect/no-non-throwing-schema-sync-decoder-outside-consumer`
  reserves `Result`/`Exit`/`Option` decoders for configured synchronous
  consumers, tests, and deterministic fixtures.
- `effect/no-unknown-tagged-error-payload`: rejects `Schema.Unknown` in any
  imported or aliased `Schema.TaggedError` payload field. It intentionally
  does not infer arbitrary serializable outputs or follow unrelated local
  identifiers.

# Anti-slop and Effect TS hardening plan

## Purpose

Implement the approved
[anti-slop and Effect TS hardening SPEC](../../product-specs/anti-slop-effect-ts-hardening/SPEC.md)
on `codex/anti-slop-effect-ts` and leave a committed branch ready for review.

## Scope

- Complete the vendored anti-slop migration.
- Keep useful JavaScript redeclaration protection and correct its TypeScript
  scope.
- Replace all module mocking with Effect services, Layers, Scope, and
  `@effect/vitest`.
- Migrate to the current compatible Effect TS and Oxlint component set.
- Resolve all anti-slop findings and reconcile owning documentation.

No push, PR creation, deployment, provider read/write, credential operation,
or hosted/public claim is authorised.

## Call graphs

```ts
bun run check
  -> Ultracite
    -> @effect/tsgo-patched Oxlint
      -> official Effect TS preset + Site plugins + anti-slop plugins

@effect/vitest
  -> scoped test Effect
    -> production service contract
      -> controlled test Layer
```

- [x] Created goal and `codex/anti-slop-effect-ts` from current `origin/main`

# Anti-slop and Effect TS hardening

## Overview

This SPEC completes the repository-wide adoption of Dillon Mulroy's vendored
anti-slop rules and moves Site from `@effect/language-service` to the current
`@effect/tsgo` Oxlint integration. It keeps useful JavaScript redeclaration
checking, removes module mocking, and resolves every anti-slop diagnostic by
correcting ownership, naming, decoding, or exact tooling scope.

## Problem

The initial anti-slop installation correctly enabled every generic rule and the
optional Effect service-constructor rule. The first full check exposed four
separate concerns:

1. Ultracite's JavaScript `eslint/no-redeclare` rule is applied to valid
   TypeScript value/type pairs, including Effect Schema declarations.
2. Fourteen tests replace whole modules with `vi.mock` or `vi.doMock` instead
   of substituting typed capabilities through Effect Layers.
3. The remaining anti-slop diagnostics identify unknown boundary ownership,
   runtime `typeof` checks, and `makeX` names or imports that conflict with the
   Effect service-constructor convention.
4. Site still uses the retired JavaScript language-service patch while current
   Effect TS diagnostics integrate directly with TypeScript-Go and Oxlint.

## Goals

1. Keep `eslint/no-redeclare` enabled for JavaScript and disable that
   JavaScript-only rule for TypeScript, where `tsc` owns real declaration
   errors and valid value/type pairs must remain accepted.
2. Add an executable regression fixture proving duplicate JavaScript bindings
   fail while an Effect Schema value/type pair passes.
3. Remove every `vi.mock`, `vi.doMock`, Jest module mock, and equivalent module
   replacement from owned tests.
4. Use `@effect/vitest`, scoped resources, service contracts, and deterministic
   test Layers for substitutable provider, browser, transport, and runtime
   capabilities.
5. Resolve every remaining `anti-slop/*` and
   `anti-slop-effect/*` diagnostic without unsafe casts, type laundering,
   broad ignores, or lowered severity.
6. Replace `@effect/language-service` with `@effect/tsgo` 0.37.0 and its
   supported TypeScript 7.0.2, Oxlint 1.80.0, and `oxlint-tsgolint` 7.0.2001
   components. Keep the application runtime Effect and `@effect/vitest`
   packages on their existing compatible beta.100 family.
7. Run the official Effect TS Oxlint preset together with Site's existing
   Ultracite and repository-local rules, resolving conflicting or duplicate
   ownership explicitly.

## Non-goals

- No route, content, public API, provider, deployment, credential, Cloudflare,
  Alchemy, Axiom, GitHub, or production mutation.
- No broad lint disable, warning demotion, new suppression comment, unsafe
  assertion, local DTO mirror, manual unknown reader, or generic test utility.
- No service or Layer for a pure function that has no substitutable capability
  or resource lifetime.
- No claim that local checks prove hosted CI, Preview, Production, or provider
  behaviour.

## Ownership and boundaries

- `package.json`, `bun.lock`, `tsconfig.base.json`, and `oxlint.config.ts` own
  the executable toolchain and rule scopes.
- `tools/oxlint/fixtures.test.ts` plus exact fixtures own regression proof for
  the TypeScript redeclaration correction and anti-slop integration.
- Existing package and app service contracts own production capabilities.
  Tests provide controlled Layers for those contracts; test-only observation
  and fault injection stay in separate test control services where needed.
- Third-party Playwright, Lighthouse, Chrome launcher, Node socket, TanStack
  devtools, and app-runtime imports stay private to live or host adapters.
- `docs/standards/tooling.md`, `docs/architecture/effect-services.md`, and
  `docs/architecture/testing-and-quality.md` own durable policy and commands.

## Proposed approach

### Toolchain

Install the exact component set published by `@effect/tsgo` 0.37.0:

- TypeScript 7.0.2;
- Oxlint 1.80.0;
- `oxlint-tsgolint` 7.0.2001; and
- `@oxlint/plugins` 1.80.0 for the vendored JavaScript plugins.

Remove `@effect/language-service`, use `effect-tsgo patch --oxlint`, and extend
Oxlint with the official recommended Effect TS preset. Keep Effect,
`@effect/platform-bun`, `@effect/platform-node`, and `@effect/vitest` on the
same beta.100 family. A runtime Effect API upgrade is a separate migration.

### Redeclaration policy

Keep `eslint/no-redeclare` at error severity for JavaScript. Add an exact
TypeScript-family override that disables this JavaScript rule for
`*.ts`, `*.tsx`, `*.mts`, and `*.cts`. TypeScript 7 remains responsible for
invalid TypeScript declarations. A real Oxlint fixture must prove both sides of
the policy.

### Test substitution

Replace module replacement with dependency substitution:

- production code yields a named service;
- live Layers import and call the third-party module;
- tests provide a memory or controlled Layer with the same contract;
- `@effect/vitest` owns Effect execution, Scope, TestClock, and finalisation;
- test-control services record calls and inject expected failures without
  adding test-only methods to production contracts.

### Remaining anti-slop findings

- Decode raw input at the real ingress, then pass schema-derived values to pure
  policy functions.
- Rename non-service `makeX` helpers to names that describe their real work.
- Import and provide owning Layers instead of importing real service
  constructors into runtime consumers.
- Replace application `typeof` checks with Schema, `Match`, or already-decoded
  domain branches.
- Where lint-plugin implementations must inspect ESTree JavaScript values,
  use one exact documented tooling scope backed by a fixture. Do not exempt
  ordinary application or test code.

## Call graphs

### Lint and type checking

```ts
bun run check
  -> Ultracite
    -> Oxlint 1.80.0 patched by @effect/tsgo 0.37.0
      -> official effecttsgo recommended preset
      -> Site effect/bun/mdx/site plugins
      -> vendored anti-slop and anti-slop-effect plugins

bun run check-types
  -> workspace TypeScript 7.0.2 compiler
    -> schema value/type namespace semantics
    -> ordinary duplicate declaration errors
```

### Production and test substitution

```ts
Production owner
  -> yield CapabilityService
    -> CapabilityLive
      -> private Playwright/Lighthouse/Chrome/socket/runtime adapter

@effect/vitest test
  -> Effect test program in Scope
    -> CapabilityTest or CapabilityMemory
      -> deterministic response, call observation, and fault injection
```

## Risks and tradeoffs

- TypeScript 7 and the current Effect TS diagnostics can reveal real migration
  errors beyond the original lint findings. Those errors remain in scope when
  caused by this toolchain change.
- Removing module mocks may require small production ownership changes. Each
  new service must represent a real substitutable capability or resource, not
  a testing convenience wrapper.
- The official Effect TS preset may overlap with Site's syntax-only rules.
  Keep the earliest precise owner and remove or scope only proven duplicate
  diagnostics.
- Local checks cannot prove hosted CI or user-facing production behaviour.

# Anti-slop and Effect TS hardening

## Overview

This SPEC completes the repository-wide adoption of Dillon Mulroy's vendored
anti-slop rules and moves Site from `@effect/language-service` to the current
`@effect/tsgo` Oxlint integration. It keeps useful JavaScript redeclaration
checking, removes module mocking, and resolves every anti-slop diagnostic by
correcting ownership, naming, decoding, or exact tooling scope.

## Problem

The initial anti-slop installation correctly enabled every generic rule and the
optional Effect service-constructor rule. The first full check exposed four
separate concerns:

1. Ultracite's JavaScript `eslint/no-redeclare` rule is applied to valid
   TypeScript value/type pairs, including Effect Schema declarations.
2. Fourteen tests replace whole modules with `vi.mock` or `vi.doMock` instead
   of substituting typed capabilities through Effect Layers.
3. The remaining anti-slop diagnostics identify unknown boundary ownership,
   runtime `typeof` checks, and `makeX` names or imports that conflict with the
   Effect service-constructor convention.
4. Site still uses the retired JavaScript language-service patch while current
   Effect TS diagnostics integrate directly with TypeScript-Go and Oxlint.

## Goals

1. Keep `eslint/no-redeclare` enabled for JavaScript and disable that
   JavaScript-only rule for TypeScript, where `tsc` owns real declaration
   errors and valid value/type pairs must remain accepted.
2. Add an executable regression fixture proving duplicate JavaScript bindings
   fail while an Effect Schema value/type pair passes.
3. Remove every `vi.mock`, `vi.doMock`, Jest module mock, and equivalent module
   replacement from owned tests.
4. Use `@effect/vitest`, scoped resources, service contracts, and deterministic
   test Layers for substitutable provider, browser, transport, and runtime
   capabilities.
5. Resolve every remaining `anti-slop/*` and
   `anti-slop-effect/*` diagnostic without unsafe casts, type laundering,
   broad ignores, or lowered severity.
6. Replace `@effect/language-service` with `@effect/tsgo` 0.37.0 and its
   supported TypeScript 7.0.2, Oxlint 1.80.0, and `oxlint-tsgolint` 7.0.2001
   components. Keep the application runtime Effect and `@effect/vitest`
   packages on their existing compatible beta.100 family.
7. Run the official Effect TS Oxlint preset together with Site's existing
   Ultracite and repository-local rules, resolving conflicting or duplicate
   ownership explicitly.

## Non-goals

- No route, content, public API, provider, deployment, credential, Cloudflare,
  Alchemy, Axiom, GitHub, or production mutation.
- No broad lint disable, warning demotion, new suppression comment, unsafe
  assertion, local DTO mirror, manual unknown reader, or generic test utility.
- No service or Layer for a pure function that has no substitutable capability
  or resource lifetime.
- No claim that local checks prove hosted CI, Preview, Production, or provider
  behaviour.

## Ownership and boundaries

- `package.json`, `bun.lock`, `tsconfig.base.json`, and `oxlint.config.ts` own
  the executable toolchain and rule scopes.
- `tools/oxlint/fixtures.test.ts` plus exact fixtures own regression proof for
  the TypeScript redeclaration correction and anti-slop integration.
- Existing package and app service contracts own production capabilities.
  Tests provide controlled Layers for those contracts; test-only observation
  and fault injection stay in separate test control services where needed.
- Third-party Playwright, Lighthouse, Chrome launcher, Node socket, TanStack
  devtools, and app-runtime imports stay private to live or host adapters.
- `docs/standards/tooling.md`, `docs/architecture/effect-services.md`, and
  `docs/architecture/testing-and-quality.md` own durable policy and commands.

## Proposed approach

### Toolchain

Install the exact component set published by `@effect/tsgo` 0.37.0:

- TypeScript 7.0.2;
- Oxlint 1.80.0;
- `oxlint-tsgolint` 7.0.2001; and
- `@oxlint/plugins` 1.80.0 for the vendored JavaScript plugins.

Remove `@effect/language-service`, use `effect-tsgo patch --oxlint`, and extend
Oxlint with the official recommended Effect TS preset. Keep Effect,
`@effect/platform-bun`, `@effect/platform-node`, and `@effect/vitest` on the
same beta.100 family. A runtime Effect API upgrade is a separate migration.

### Redeclaration policy

Keep `eslint/no-redeclare` at error severity for JavaScript. Add an exact
TypeScript-family override that disables this JavaScript rule for
`*.ts`, `*.tsx`, `*.mts`, and `*.cts`. TypeScript 7 remains responsible for
invalid TypeScript declarations. A real Oxlint fixture must prove both sides of
the policy.

### Test substitution

Replace module replacement with dependency substitution:

- production code yields a named service;
- live Layers import and call the third-party module;
- tests provide a memory or controlled Layer with the same contract;
- `@effect/vitest` owns Effect execution, Scope, TestClock, and finalisation;
- test-control services record calls and inject expected failures without
  adding test-only methods to production contracts.

### Remaining anti-slop findings

- Decode raw input at the real ingress, then pass schema-derived values to pure
  policy functions.
- Rename non-service `makeX` helpers to names that describe their real work.
- Import and provide owning Layers instead of importing real service
  constructors into runtime consumers.
- Replace application `typeof` checks with Schema, `Match`, or already-decoded
  domain branches.
- Where lint-plugin implementations must inspect ESTree JavaScript values,
  use one exact documented tooling scope backed by a fixture. Do not exempt
  ordinary application or test code.

## Call graphs

### Lint and type checking

```ts
bun run check
  -> Ultracite
    -> Oxlint 1.80.0 patched by @effect/tsgo 0.37.0
      -> official effecttsgo recommended preset
      -> Site effect/bun/mdx/site plugins
      -> vendored anti-slop and anti-slop-effect plugins

bun run check-types
  -> workspace TypeScript 7.0.2 compiler
    -> schema value/type namespace semantics
    -> ordinary duplicate declaration errors
```

### Production and test substitution

```ts
Production owner
  -> yield CapabilityService
    -> CapabilityLive
      -> private Playwright/Lighthouse/Chrome/socket/runtime adapter

@effect/vitest test
  -> Effect test program in Scope
    -> CapabilityTest or CapabilityMemory
      -> deterministic response, call observation, and fault injection
```

## Risks and tradeoffs

- TypeScript 7 and the current Effect TS diagnostics can reveal real migration
  errors beyond the original lint findings. Those errors remain in scope when
  caused by this toolchain change.
- Removing module mocks may require small production ownership changes. Each
  new service must represent a real substitutable capability or resource, not
  a testing convenience wrapper.
- The official Effect TS preset may overlap with Site's syntax-only rules.
  Keep the earliest precise owner and remove or scope only proven duplicate
  diagnostics.
- Local checks cannot prove hosted CI or user-facing production behaviour.

## Documentation impact ledger

| ------------------------ | --------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `docs`                   | Change required | This SPEC, active plan, and the three durable tooling/testing owners named above.                                       |
| `readmes`                | Preserve        | Root and package commands/consumer exports remain unchanged unless an implementation slice changes one.                 |
| `architecture_standards` | Change required | `docs/standards/tooling.md`, `docs/architecture/effect-services.md`, and `docs/architecture/testing-and-quality.md`.    |
| `runbooks`               | N/A             | No repeatable provider or operational procedure changes.                                                                |
| `proof_evidence`         | Change required | Active-plan validation log records exact local candidate and checks; no hosted or provider proof.                       |
| `skills`                 | Preserve        | The vendored install and repository skills remain unchanged; this work consumes them.                                   |
| `lint_config_ci`         | Change required | Root manifest, lockfile, TypeScript config, Oxlint config, and existing root commands.                                  |

## Acceptance criteria

- `rg` finds no owned module mocking calls.
- Every anti-slop and anti-slop-effect rule remains enabled at error severity.
- Duplicate JavaScript declarations fail the lint fixture and valid TypeScript

# Anti-slop and Effect TS hardening plan

## Purpose

Implement the approved
[anti-slop and Effect TS hardening SPEC](../../product-specs/anti-slop-effect-ts-hardening/SPEC.md)
on `codex/anti-slop-effect-ts` and leave a committed branch ready for review.

## Scope

- Complete the vendored anti-slop migration.
- Keep useful JavaScript redeclaration protection and correct its TypeScript
  scope.
- Replace all module mocking with Effect services, Layers, Scope, and
  `@effect/vitest`.
- Migrate to the current compatible Effect TS and Oxlint component set.
- Resolve all anti-slop findings and reconcile owning documentation.

No push, PR creation, deployment, provider read/write, credential operation,
or hosted/public claim is authorised.

## Call graphs

```ts
bun run check
  -> Ultracite
    -> @effect/tsgo-patched Oxlint
      -> official Effect TS preset + Site plugins + anti-slop plugins

@effect/vitest
  -> scoped test Effect
    -> production service contract
      -> controlled test Layer
```

## Progress

- [x] Created goal and `codex/anti-slop-effect-ts` from current `origin/main`
      commit `321164bc`.
- [x] Carried the committed anti-slop installer slice as commit `9c7fc7c1`.
- [x] Verified published component metadata for `@effect/tsgo` 0.37.0:
      TypeScript 7.0.2, Oxlint 1.80.0, and `oxlint-tsgolint` 7.0.2001.
- [x] ASL-001 toolchain migration and focused proof.
- [x] ASL-002 TypeScript redeclaration correction and fixtures.
- [x] ASL-003 module-mock replacement.
- [x] ASL-004 remaining anti-slop findings.
- [x] ASL-005 local closeout and lifecycle transition, with the retained
      historical-attestation limitation below.

## Discoveries

- The original install skill and vendored source match Dillon Mulroy's current
  upstream setup. Installation is not the cause of the residual findings.
- The 345 `eslint/no-redeclare` diagnostics come from Ultracite's JavaScript
  core rule applied to TypeScript. They are outside the anti-slop plugin.
- The original partial follow-up work remains uncommitted and preserved in its
  separate worktree. It was not copied because its lint-fixture changes filtered
  unrelated diagnostics instead of retaining the complete fixture oracle.
- `@effect/tsgo` 0.37.0 embeds the exact current Oxlint component versions
  already selected by the installer.

## Decision log

- Keep `eslint/no-redeclare` for JavaScript. Disable only that JavaScript rule
  for TypeScript-family files and prove both behaviours with the real linter.
- Adopt the official recommended Effect TS Oxlint preset. Resolve overlaps at
  the earliest precise owner instead of running two competing diagnostics.
- Treat module mocks as architecture findings. Tests will use controlled Layers
  over real contracts and `@effect/vitest` Scope.
- Exact lint-plugin implementation scope may admit JavaScript representation
  inspection only when a real fixture proves the boundary. Application and test
  code receive no matching exemption.

## Validation log

- `npm view`: current `@effect/tsgo` is 0.37.0; current Oxlint and
  `@oxlint/plugins` are 1.80.0; current `oxlint-tsgolint` is 7.0.2001;
  current TypeScript is 7.0.2.
- Published `@effect/tsgo` metadata confirms those TypeScript/Oxlint component
  versions. Its package development family is Effect beta.107, but it has no
  Effect peer dependency and supports Effect v4.
- The attempted runtime Effect beta.107 upgrade failed immediately because
  that release removes `Schema.TaggedErrorClass`. Site remains on its existing
  internally matched beta.100 runtime family; a runtime API upgrade is outside
  this lint and test-substitution migration.
- Baseline anti-slop branch: workspace typecheck passed before migration;
  `bun run check` remained red with the known redeclaration and anti-slop
  findings. This is baseline evidence, not completion proof.

## Documentation impact ledger

The SPEC owns the complete impact ledger. Current required owners are the root

# Anti-slop and Effect TS hardening

## Overview

This SPEC completes the repository-wide adoption of Dillon Mulroy's vendored
anti-slop rules and moves Site from `@effect/language-service` to the current
`@effect/tsgo` Oxlint integration. It keeps useful JavaScript redeclaration
checking, removes module mocking, and resolves every anti-slop diagnostic by
correcting ownership, naming, decoding, or exact tooling scope.

## Problem

The initial anti-slop installation correctly enabled every generic rule and the
optional Effect service-constructor rule. The first full check exposed four
separate concerns:

1. Ultracite's JavaScript `eslint/no-redeclare` rule is applied to valid
   TypeScript value/type pairs, including Effect Schema declarations.
2. Fourteen tests replace whole modules with `vi.mock` or `vi.doMock` instead
   of substituting typed capabilities through Effect Layers.
3. The remaining anti-slop diagnostics identify unknown boundary ownership,
   runtime `typeof` checks, and `makeX` names or imports that conflict with the
   Effect service-constructor convention.
4. Site still uses the retired JavaScript language-service patch while current
   Effect TS diagnostics integrate directly with TypeScript-Go and Oxlint.

## Goals

1. Keep `eslint/no-redeclare` enabled for JavaScript and disable that
   JavaScript-only rule for TypeScript, where `tsc` owns real declaration
   errors and valid value/type pairs must remain accepted.
2. Add an executable regression fixture proving duplicate JavaScript bindings
   fail while an Effect Schema value/type pair passes.
3. Remove every `vi.mock`, `vi.doMock`, Jest module mock, and equivalent module
   replacement from owned tests.
4. Use `@effect/vitest`, scoped resources, service contracts, and deterministic
   test Layers for substitutable provider, browser, transport, and runtime
   capabilities.
5. Resolve every remaining `anti-slop/*` and
   `anti-slop-effect/*` diagnostic without unsafe casts, type laundering,
   broad ignores, or lowered severity.
6. Replace `@effect/language-service` with `@effect/tsgo` 0.37.0 and its
   supported TypeScript 7.0.2, Oxlint 1.80.0, and `oxlint-tsgolint` 7.0.2001
   components. Keep the application runtime Effect and `@effect/vitest`
   packages on their existing compatible beta.100 family.
7. Run the official Effect TS Oxlint preset together with Site's existing
   Ultracite and repository-local rules, resolving conflicting or duplicate
   ownership explicitly.

## Non-goals

- No route, content, public API, provider, deployment, credential, Cloudflare,
  Alchemy, Axiom, GitHub, or production mutation.
- No broad lint disable, warning demotion, new suppression comment, unsafe
  assertion, local DTO mirror, manual unknown reader, or generic test utility.
- No service or Layer for a pure function that has no substitutable capability
  or resource lifetime.
- No claim that local checks prove hosted CI, Preview, Production, or provider
  behaviour.

## Ownership and boundaries

- `package.json`, `bun.lock`, `tsconfig.base.json`, and `oxlint.config.ts` own
  the executable toolchain and rule scopes.
- `tools/oxlint/fixtures.test.ts` plus exact fixtures own regression proof for
  the TypeScript redeclaration correction and anti-slop integration.
- Existing package and app service contracts own production capabilities.
  Tests provide controlled Layers for those contracts; test-only observation
  and fault injection stay in separate test control services where needed.
- Third-party Playwright, Lighthouse, Chrome launcher, Node socket, TanStack
  devtools, and app-runtime imports stay private to live or host adapters.
- `docs/standards/tooling.md`, `docs/architecture/effect-services.md`, and
  `docs/architecture/testing-and-quality.md` own durable policy and commands.

## Proposed approach

### Toolchain

Install the exact component set published by `@effect/tsgo` 0.37.0:

- TypeScript 7.0.2;
- Oxlint 1.80.0;
- `oxlint-tsgolint` 7.0.2001; and
- `@oxlint/plugins` 1.80.0 for the vendored JavaScript plugins.

Remove `@effect/language-service`, use `effect-tsgo patch --oxlint`, and extend
Oxlint with the official recommended Effect TS preset. Keep Effect,
`@effect/platform-bun`, `@effect/platform-node`, and `@effect/vitest` on the
same beta.100 family. A runtime Effect API upgrade is a separate migration.

### Redeclaration policy

Keep `eslint/no-redeclare` at error severity for JavaScript. Add an exact
TypeScript-family override that disables this JavaScript rule for
`*.ts`, `*.tsx`, `*.mts`, and `*.cts`. TypeScript 7 remains responsible for
invalid TypeScript declarations. A real Oxlint fixture must prove both sides of
the policy.

### Test substitution

Replace module replacement with dependency substitution:

- production code yields a named service;
- live Layers import and call the third-party module;
- tests provide a memory or controlled Layer with the same contract;
- `@effect/vitest` owns Effect execution, Scope, TestClock, and finalisation;
- test-control services record calls and inject expected failures without
  adding test-only methods to production contracts.

### Remaining anti-slop findings

- Decode raw input at the real ingress, then pass schema-derived values to pure
  policy functions.
- Rename non-service `makeX` helpers to names that describe their real work.
- Import and provide owning Layers instead of importing real service
  constructors into runtime consumers.
- Replace application `typeof` checks with Schema, `Match`, or already-decoded
  domain branches.
- Where lint-plugin implementations must inspect ESTree JavaScript values,
  use one exact documented tooling scope backed by a fixture. Do not exempt
  ordinary application or test code.

## Call graphs

### Lint and type checking

```ts
bun run check
  -> Ultracite
    -> Oxlint 1.80.0 patched by @effect/tsgo 0.37.0
      -> official effecttsgo recommended preset
      -> Site effect/bun/mdx/site plugins
      -> vendored anti-slop and anti-slop-effect plugins

bun run check-types
  -> workspace TypeScript 7.0.2 compiler
    -> schema value/type namespace semantics
    -> ordinary duplicate declaration errors
```

### Production and test substitution

```ts
Production owner
  -> yield CapabilityService
    -> CapabilityLive
      -> private Playwright/Lighthouse/Chrome/socket/runtime adapter

@effect/vitest test
  -> Effect test program in Scope
    -> CapabilityTest or CapabilityMemory
      -> deterministic response, call observation, and fault injection
```

## Risks and tradeoffs

- TypeScript 7 and the current Effect TS diagnostics can reveal real migration
  errors beyond the original lint findings. Those errors remain in scope when
  caused by this toolchain change.
- Removing module mocks may require small production ownership changes. Each
  new service must represent a real substitutable capability or resource, not
  a testing convenience wrapper.
- The official Effect TS preset may overlap with Site's syntax-only rules.
  Keep the earliest precise owner and remove or scope only proven duplicate
  diagnostics.
- Local checks cannot prove hosted CI or user-facing production behaviour.

# Anti-slop and Effect TS hardening

## Overview

This SPEC completes the repository-wide adoption of Dillon Mulroy's vendored
anti-slop rules and moves Site from `@effect/language-service` to the current
`@effect/tsgo` Oxlint integration. It keeps useful JavaScript redeclaration
checking, removes module mocking, and resolves every anti-slop diagnostic by
correcting ownership, naming, decoding, or exact tooling scope.

## Problem

The initial anti-slop installation correctly enabled every generic rule and the
optional Effect service-constructor rule. The first full check exposed four
separate concerns:

1. Ultracite's JavaScript `eslint/no-redeclare` rule is applied to valid
   TypeScript value/type pairs, including Effect Schema declarations.
2. Fourteen tests replace whole modules with `vi.mock` or `vi.doMock` instead
   of substituting typed capabilities through Effect Layers.
3. The remaining anti-slop diagnostics identify unknown boundary ownership,
   runtime `typeof` checks, and `makeX` names or imports that conflict with the
   Effect service-constructor convention.
4. Site still uses the retired JavaScript language-service patch while current
   Effect TS diagnostics integrate directly with TypeScript-Go and Oxlint.

## Goals

1. Keep `eslint/no-redeclare` enabled for JavaScript and disable that
   JavaScript-only rule for TypeScript, where `tsc` owns real declaration
   errors and valid value/type pairs must remain accepted.
2. Add an executable regression fixture proving duplicate JavaScript bindings
   fail while an Effect Schema value/type pair passes.
3. Remove every `vi.mock`, `vi.doMock`, Jest module mock, and equivalent module
   replacement from owned tests.
4. Use `@effect/vitest`, scoped resources, service contracts, and deterministic
   test Layers for substitutable provider, browser, transport, and runtime
   capabilities.
5. Resolve every remaining `anti-slop/*` and
   `anti-slop-effect/*` diagnostic without unsafe casts, type laundering,
   broad ignores, or lowered severity.
6. Replace `@effect/language-service` with `@effect/tsgo` 0.37.0 and its
   supported TypeScript 7.0.2, Oxlint 1.80.0, and `oxlint-tsgolint` 7.0.2001
   components. Keep the application runtime Effect and `@effect/vitest`
   packages on their existing compatible beta.100 family.
7. Run the official Effect TS Oxlint preset together with Site's existing
   Ultracite and repository-local rules, resolving conflicting or duplicate
   ownership explicitly.

## Non-goals

- No route, content, public API, provider, deployment, credential, Cloudflare,
  Alchemy, Axiom, GitHub, or production mutation.
- No broad lint disable, warning demotion, new suppression comment, unsafe
  assertion, local DTO mirror, manual unknown reader, or generic test utility.
- No service or Layer for a pure function that has no substitutable capability
  or resource lifetime.
- No claim that local checks prove hosted CI, Preview, Production, or provider
  behaviour.

## Ownership and boundaries

- `package.json`, `bun.lock`, `tsconfig.base.json`, and `oxlint.config.ts` own
  the executable toolchain and rule scopes.
- `tools/oxlint/fixtures.test.ts` plus exact fixtures own regression proof for
  the TypeScript redeclaration correction and anti-slop integration.
- Existing package and app service contracts own production capabilities.
  Tests provide controlled Layers for those contracts; test-only observation
  and fault injection stay in separate test control services where needed.
- Third-party Playwright, Lighthouse, Chrome launcher, Node socket, TanStack
  devtools, and app-runtime imports stay private to live or host adapters.
- `docs/standards/tooling.md`, `docs/architecture/effect-services.md`, and
  `docs/architecture/testing-and-quality.md` own durable policy and commands.

## Proposed approach

### Toolchain

Install the exact component set published by `@effect/tsgo` 0.37.0:

- TypeScript 7.0.2;
- Oxlint 1.80.0;
- `oxlint-tsgolint` 7.0.2001; and
- `@oxlint/plugins` 1.80.0 for the vendored JavaScript plugins.

Remove `@effect/language-service`, use `effect-tsgo patch --oxlint`, and extend
Oxlint with the official recommended Effect TS preset. Keep Effect,
`@effect/platform-bun`, `@effect/platform-node`, and `@effect/vitest` on the
same beta.100 family. A runtime Effect API upgrade is a separate migration.

### Redeclaration policy

Keep `eslint/no-redeclare` at error severity for JavaScript. Add an exact
TypeScript-family override that disables this JavaScript rule for
`*.ts`, `*.tsx`, `*.mts`, and `*.cts`. TypeScript 7 remains responsible for
invalid TypeScript declarations. A real Oxlint fixture must prove both sides of
the policy.

### Test substitution

Replace module replacement with dependency substitution:

- production code yields a named service;
- live Layers import and call the third-party module;
- tests provide a memory or controlled Layer with the same contract;
- `@effect/vitest` owns Effect execution, Scope, TestClock, and finalisation;
- test-control services record calls and inject expected failures without
  adding test-only methods to production contracts.

### Remaining anti-slop findings

- Decode raw input at the real ingress, then pass schema-derived values to pure
  policy functions.
- Rename non-service `makeX` helpers to names that describe their real work.
- Import and provide owning Layers instead of importing real service
  constructors into runtime consumers.
- Replace application `typeof` checks with Schema, `Match`, or already-decoded
  domain branches.
- Where lint-plugin implementations must inspect ESTree JavaScript values,
  use one exact documented tooling scope backed by a fixture. Do not exempt
  ordinary application or test code.

## Call graphs

### Lint and type checking

```ts
bun run check
  -> Ultracite
    -> Oxlint 1.80.0 patched by @effect/tsgo 0.37.0
      -> official effecttsgo recommended preset
      -> Site effect/bun/mdx/site plugins
      -> vendored anti-slop and anti-slop-effect plugins

bun run check-types
  -> workspace TypeScript 7.0.2 compiler
    -> schema value/type namespace semantics
    -> ordinary duplicate declaration errors
```

### Production and test substitution

```ts
Production owner
  -> yield CapabilityService
    -> CapabilityLive
      -> private Playwright/Lighthouse/Chrome/socket/runtime adapter

@effect/vitest test
  -> Effect test program in Scope
    -> CapabilityTest or CapabilityMemory
      -> deterministic response, call observation, and fault injection
```

## Risks and tradeoffs

- TypeScript 7 and the current Effect TS diagnostics can reveal real migration
  errors beyond the original lint findings. Those errors remain in scope when
  caused by this toolchain change.
- Removing module mocks may require small production ownership changes. Each
  new service must represent a real substitutable capability or resource, not
  a testing convenience wrapper.
- The official Effect TS preset may overlap with Site's syntax-only rules.
  Keep the earliest precise owner and remove or scope only proven duplicate
  diagnostics.
- Local checks cannot prove hosted CI or user-facing production behaviour.

## Acceptance criteria

- `rg` finds no owned module mocking calls.
- Every anti-slop and anti-slop-effect rule remains enabled at error severity.
- Duplicate JavaScript declarations fail the lint fixture and valid TypeScript

import { spawnSync } from "node:child_process";
import { rmSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs";
import nodePath from "node:path";

import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest";

import { deterministicEffectNativeVitestFixture } from "../packages/codex/test/fixtures/effect-native-vitest-positive.js";

const { resolve } = nodePath;

const runFixture = (fixture: string) => {
  const child = spawnSync(
    "bunx",
    [
      "--bun",
      "oxlint",
      "--config",
      "lint/fixtures/effect-native.config.json",
      fixture,
    ],
    { encoding: "utf-8" }
  );
  return {
    exitCode: child.status,
    output: `${child.stdout}\n${child.stderr}`,
  };
};

describe("installed Bundjil Oxlint plugin", () => {
  it("accepts the exact positive fixture", () => {
    const result = runFixture("lint/fixtures/effect-native-positive.ts");
    expect(result.exitCode).toBe(0);
    expect(result.output).not.toContain("bundjil(");
  });

  it("accepts the Effect TestClock fixture through installed Oxlint", () => {
    const result = runFixture(
      "lint/fixtures/effect-native-test-clock-positive.ts"
    );
    expect(result.exitCode).toBe(0);
    expect(result.output).not.toContain("bundjil(");
  });

  it("accepts the package-resolved @effect/vitest fixture", () => {
    expect(deterministicEffectNativeVitestFixture).toBeDefined();
    const result = runFixture(
      "packages/codex/test/fixtures/effect-native-vitest-positive.ts"
    );
    expect(result.exitCode).toBe(0);
    expect(result.output).not.toContain("bundjil(");
  });

  it("rejects every exact negative rule fixture by stable ID", () => {
    const result = runFixture("lint/fixtures/effect-native-negative.ts");
    expect(result.exitCode).not.toBe(0);
    for (const rule of [
      "bundjil(no-ambient-time-in-effect)",
      "bundjil(no-async-await-in-effect-service)",
      "bundjil(no-exported-effect-gen-function)",
      "bundjil(no-layer-or-die-in-service)",
      "bundjil(no-primitive-effect-failure)",
      "bundjil(no-runtime-execution-outside-boundary)",
      "bundjil(no-unregistered-native-collection)",
      "bundjil(require-try-promise-catch)",
    ]) {
      expect(result.output).toContain(rule);
    }
  });

  it("applies ambient-time enforcement to owned tooling", () => {
    const probe = "tooling/.ambient-time-lint-probe.ts";
    writeFileSync(resolve(probe), "new Date();\n");

    try {
      const child = spawnSync(
        "bunx",
        ["--bun", "oxlint", "--config", "oxlint.config.ts", probe],
        { encoding: "utf-8" }
      );
      expect(child.status).not.toBe(0);
      expect(`${child.stdout}\n${child.stderr}`).toContain(
        "bundjil(no-ambient-time-in-effect)"
      );
    } finally {
      rmSync(resolve(probe), { force: true });
    }
  });

  it("applies primitive-failure enforcement to infrastructure scripts", () => {
    const probe =
      "packages/infrastructure/scripts/.primitive-failure-lint-probe.ts";
    writeFileSync(
      resolve(probe),
      'import { Effect } from "effect";\nEffect.fail("primitive");\n'
    );

    try {
      const child = spawnSync(
        "bunx",
        ["--bun", "oxlint", "--config", "oxlint.config.ts", probe],
        { encoding: "utf-8" }
      );
      expect(child.status).not.toBe(0);
      expect(`${child.stdout}\n${child.stderr}`).toContain(
        "bundjil(no-primitive-effect-failure)"
      );
    } finally {
      rmSync(resolve(probe), { force: true });
    }
  });

  it("applies native-collection review to owned package scripts", () => {
    const probe =
      "packages/infrastructure/scripts/.native-collection-lint-probe.ts";
    writeFileSync(resolve(probe), 'const values = new Set(["value"]);\n');

      expect(`${child.stdout}\n${child.stderr}`).toContain(
        "bundjil(no-unregistered-native-collection)"
      );
    } finally {
      rmSync(resolve(probe), { force: true });
    }
  });
});

import { spawnSync } from "node:child_process";
import { rmSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs";
import nodePath from "node:path";

import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest";

import { deterministicEffectNativeVitestFixture } from "../packages/codex/test/fixtures/effect-native-vitest-positive.js";

const { resolve } = nodePath;

const runFixture = (fixture: string) => {
  const child = spawnSync(
    "bunx",
    [
      "--bun",
      "oxlint",
      "--config",
      "lint/fixtures/effect-native.config.json",
      fixture,
    ],
    { encoding: "utf-8" }
  );
  return {
    exitCode: child.status,
    output: `${child.stdout}\n${child.stderr}`,
  };
};

describe("installed Bundjil Oxlint plugin", () => {
  it("accepts the exact positive fixture", () => {
    const result = runFixture("lint/fixtures/effect-native-positive.ts");
    expect(result.exitCode).toBe(0);
    expect(result.output).not.toContain("bundjil(");
  });

  it("accepts the Effect TestClock fixture through installed Oxlint", () => {
    const result = runFixture(
      "lint/fixtures/effect-native-test-clock-positive.ts"
    );
    expect(result.exitCode).toBe(0);
    expect(result.output).not.toContain("bundjil(");
  });

  it("accepts the package-resolved @effect/vitest fixture", () => {
    expect(deterministicEffectNativeVitestFixture).toBeDefined();
    const result = runFixture(
      "packages/codex/test/fixtures/effect-native-vitest-positive.ts"
    );
    expect(result.exitCode).toBe(0);
    expect(result.output).not.toContain("bundjil(");
  });

  it("rejects every exact negative rule fixture by stable ID", () => {
    const result = runFixture("lint/fixtures/effect-native-negative.ts");
    expect(result.exitCode).not.toBe(0);
    for (const rule of [
      "bundjil(no-ambient-time-in-effect)",
      "bundjil(no-async-await-in-effect-service)",
      "bundjil(no-exported-effect-gen-function)",
      "bundjil(no-layer-or-die-in-service)",
      "bundjil(no-primitive-effect-failure)",
      "bundjil(no-runtime-execution-outside-boundary)",
      "bundjil(no-unregistered-native-collection)",
      "bundjil(require-try-promise-catch)",
    ]) {
      expect(result.output).toContain(rule);
    }
  });

  it("applies ambient-time enforcement to owned tooling", () => {
    const probe = "tooling/.ambient-time-lint-probe.ts";
    writeFileSync(resolve(probe), "new Date();\n");

    try {
      const child = spawnSync(
        "bunx",
        ["--bun", "oxlint", "--config", "oxlint.config.ts", probe],
        { encoding: "utf-8" }
      );
      expect(child.status).not.toBe(0);
      expect(`${child.stdout}\n${child.stderr}`).toContain(
        "bundjil(no-ambient-time-in-effect)"
      );
    } finally {
      rmSync(resolve(probe), { force: true });
    }
  });

  it("applies primitive-failure enforcement to infrastructure scripts", () => {
    const probe =
      "packages/infrastructure/scripts/.primitive-failure-lint-probe.ts";
    writeFileSync(
      resolve(probe),
      'import { Effect } from "effect";\nEffect.fail("primitive");\n'
    );

    try {
      const child = spawnSync(
        "bunx",
        ["--bun", "oxlint", "--config", "oxlint.config.ts", probe],
        { encoding: "utf-8" }
      );
      expect(child.status).not.toBe(0);
      expect(`${child.stdout}\n${child.stderr}`).toContain(
        "bundjil(no-primitive-effect-failure)"
      );
    } finally {
      rmSync(resolve(probe), { force: true });
    }
  });

  it("applies native-collection review to owned package scripts", () => {
    const probe =
      "packages/infrastructure/scripts/.native-collection-lint-probe.ts";
    writeFileSync(resolve(probe), 'const values = new Set(["value"]);\n');

    try {
      const child = spawnSync(
        "bunx",
        ["--bun", "oxlint", "--config", "oxlint.config.ts", probe],
        { encoding: "utf-8" }
      );
      expect(child.status).not.toBe(0);
      expect(`${child.stdout}\n${child.stderr}`).toContain(
        "bundjil(no-unregistered-native-collection)"
      );
    } finally {
      rmSync(resolve(probe), { force: true });
    }
  });
});

import { spawnSync } from "node:child_process";
import { rmSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs";
import nodePath from "node:path";

import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest";

import { deterministicEffectNativeVitestFixture } from "../packages/codex/test/fixtures/effect-native-vitest-positive.js";

const { resolve } = nodePath;

const runFixture = (fixture: string) => {
  const child = spawnSync(
    "bunx",
    [
      "--bun",
      "oxlint",
      "--config",
      "lint/fixtures/effect-native.config.json",
      fixture,
    ],
    { encoding: "utf-8" }
  );
  return {
    exitCode: child.status,
    output: `${child.stdout}\n${child.stderr}`,
  };
};

describe("installed Bundjil Oxlint plugin", () => {
  it("accepts the exact positive fixture", () => {
    const result = runFixture("lint/fixtures/effect-native-positive.ts");
    expect(result.exitCode).toBe(0);
    expect(result.output).not.toContain("bundjil(");
  });

  it("accepts the Effect TestClock fixture through installed Oxlint", () => {
    const result = runFixture(
      "lint/fixtures/effect-native-test-clock-positive.ts"
    );
    expect(result.exitCode).toBe(0);
    expect(result.output).not.toContain("bundjil(");
  });

  it("accepts the package-resolved @effect/vitest fixture", () => {
    expect(deterministicEffectNativeVitestFixture).toBeDefined();
    const result = runFixture(
      "packages/codex/test/fixtures/effect-native-vitest-positive.ts"
    );
    expect(result.exitCode).toBe(0);
    expect(result.output).not.toContain("bundjil(");
  });

  it("rejects every exact negative rule fixture by stable ID", () => {
    const result = runFixture("lint/fixtures/effect-native-negative.ts");
    expect(result.exitCode).not.toBe(0);
    for (const rule of [
      "bundjil(no-ambient-time-in-effect)",
      "bundjil(no-async-await-in-effect-service)",
      "bundjil(no-exported-effect-gen-function)",
      "bundjil(no-layer-or-die-in-service)",
      "bundjil(no-primitive-effect-failure)",
      "bundjil(no-runtime-execution-outside-boundary)",
      "bundjil(no-unregistered-native-collection)",
      "bundjil(require-try-promise-catch)",
    ]) {
      expect(result.output).toContain(rule);
    }
  });

  it("applies ambient-time enforcement to owned tooling", () => {
    const probe = "tooling/.ambient-time-lint-probe.ts";
    writeFileSync(resolve(probe), "new Date();\n");

    try {
      const child = spawnSync(
        "bunx",
        ["--bun", "oxlint", "--config", "oxlint.config.ts", probe],
        { encoding: "utf-8" }
      );
      expect(child.status).not.toBe(0);
      expect(`${child.stdout}\n${child.stderr}`).toContain(
        "bundjil(no-ambient-time-in-effect)"
      );
    } finally {
      rmSync(resolve(probe), { force: true });
    }
  });

  it("applies primitive-failure enforcement to infrastructure scripts", () => {
    const probe =
      "packages/infrastructure/scripts/.primitive-failure-lint-probe.ts";
    writeFileSync(
      resolve(probe),
      'import { Effect } from "effect";\nEffect.fail("primitive");\n'
    );

    try {
      const child = spawnSync(
        "bunx",
        ["--bun", "oxlint", "--config", "oxlint.config.ts", probe],
        { encoding: "utf-8" }
      );
      expect(child.status).not.toBe(0);
      expect(`${child.stdout}\n${child.stderr}`).toContain(
        "bundjil(no-primitive-effect-failure)"
      );
    } finally {
      rmSync(resolve(probe), { force: true });
    }
  });

  it("applies native-collection review to owned package scripts", () => {
    const probe =
      "packages/infrastructure/scripts/.native-collection-lint-probe.ts";
    writeFileSync(resolve(probe), 'const values = new Set(["value"]);\n');

    try {
      const child = spawnSync(
        "bunx",
        ["--bun", "oxlint", "--config", "oxlint.config.ts", probe],
        { encoding: "utf-8" }
      );
      expect(child.status).not.toBe(0);
      expect(`${child.stdout}\n${child.stderr}`).toContain(
        "bundjil(no-unregistered-native-collection)"
      );
    } finally {
      rmSync(resolve(probe), { force: true });
    }
  });
});

### apps/agent/README.md
# @bundjil/agent

Committed Vercel Eve app for the Bundjil personal-agent boundary.

## Purpose and boundary

This app owns the Eve definition, app configuration, channel orchestration,
identity, routing, atomic replay, request-scoped dispatch, provider composition
roots, model selection, instructions, tools, deployment boundary, and app-level
tests.

It composes:

- `@bundjil/channel` for the provider-neutral nominal `ChannelTransport`;
- `@bundjil/sendblue` and `@bundjil/photon` only at provider-specific Layer
  composition roots;
- `@bundjil/store` for atomic replay persistence;
- `@bundjil/eve` for reusable Eve-facing contracts.

The app does not own provider wire DTOs/clients, Codex OAuth/profile storage, a
public proxy gateway, or provider management state. Provider selection does not
exist inside domain operations: each loaded authored provider module owns one
module-level runtime for its provider composition root and reuses that runtime
across invocations. The roots reuse contracts and Layer constructors but do not
share live Contexts, Scopes, build fibers, or `Layer.MemoMap` values.

## Channel boundary

Authored routes:

- `POST /eve/v1/sendblue/webhook`
- `POST /eve/v1/photon/webhook`

Each route decodes/authenticates through its provider Layer, then uses the same
identity, HMAC routing, atomic replay, immutable `ChannelStateV1`, Eve dispatch,
presence, and outbound-acceptance path. Accepted ingress returns `202`;
ignored/duplicate ingress returns `204`; authentication, payload, and
routing/replay failures map to `401`, `400`, and `503` respectively.

The shared Eve adapter prepares a request with the concrete provider runtime
and awaits the exact Eve `send()` Promise before acknowledging. It returns
`202` only after a Schema-owned safe session acceptance and an atomic
continuity fence classify the result as a new owner or intended-session
resume. A different fallback session, rejected send, or bounded handoff
timeout returns `503` and retains the inbound identity as uncertain; an exact
redelivery is suppressed. No critical work remains under `waitUntil`.
`ChannelHandoff` records only Schema-owned prepared, send, continuity,
response, terminal-session, and native Exit phases using domain-separated HMAC
work/session fingerprints and bounded timestamps/latencies. It retains no
content, raw identity, secret, error, Cause, or stack. Client disconnect does
not cancel an already-started acceptance operation; runtime disposal
interrupts it in tests without returning `202`. The adapter never constructs
or disposes a runtime per request, adds no Channel-wide retry, and does not
treat a safe fingerprint as hosted durability proof. Local Build Output and a
named deployment readback remain separate proof classes.

Pinned Eve `0.29.5` owns durable session start/resume and turn child workflows
behind its route-owned `send()` operation. Bundjil adds no second Workflow or
raw Workflow client. The test command generates ordinary and Vercel Build
Output and verifies Eve's generated Workflow `max` separately from the
ordinary function's unset duration; it makes no hosted claim. Eve creates
Nitro internally and exposes no supported app input for
`vercel.functions.maxDuration`, so a duration override requires an upstream
Eve seam rather than a guessed source glob or generated-output patch. The
handoff environment name is admitted through the Turbo build allowlist, but
the effective hosted function duration, plan and latency distributions remain
deployment readbacks.

The replacement path uses only these app-owned environment namespaces:

| Concern  | Environment names                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Handoff  | `BUNDJIL_CHANNEL_HANDOFF_TIMEOUT_MILLISECONDS` (positive Duration; 15-second product default, not a provider or Vercel requirement)                                                                                                                   |
| Routing  | `BUNDJIL_CHANNEL_ROUTING_IDENTITIES`, `BUNDJIL_CHANNEL_ROUTING_SECRET`                                                                                                                                                                                |
| Replay   | `BUNDJIL_CHANNEL_REPLAY_PREFIX`, `BUNDJIL_CHANNEL_REPLAY_LEASE_MILLISECONDS`, `BUNDJIL_CHANNEL_REPLAY_TTL_MILLISECONDS`, `BUNDJIL_CHANNEL_REPLAY_KV_REST_API_URL`, `BUNDJIL_CHANNEL_REPLAY_KV_REST_API_TOKEN`, `BUNDJIL_CHANNEL_REPLAY_STORE_PREFIX`  |
| Sendblue | `BUNDJIL_CHANNEL_SENDBLUE_ALLOWED_SERVICES`, `BUNDJIL_CHANNEL_SENDBLUE_API_KEY`, `BUNDJIL_CHANNEL_SENDBLUE_API_SECRET`, `BUNDJIL_CHANNEL_SENDBLUE_LINE`, `BUNDJIL_CHANNEL_SENDBLUE_TYPING_DURATION_MILLIS`, `BUNDJIL_CHANNEL_SENDBLUE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` |
| Photon   | `BUNDJIL_CHANNEL_PHOTON_PROJECT_ID`, `BUNDJIL_CHANNEL_PHOTON_PROJECT_SECRET`, `BUNDJIL_CHANNEL_PHOTON_WEBHOOK_ID`, `BUNDJIL_CHANNEL_PHOTON_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, `BUNDJIL_CHANNEL_PHOTON_WEBHOOK_TOLERANCE_SECONDS`                                        |
| Evidence | `EVE_TRACES_CONTENT` (Preview proof requires the encrypted value `off`; it disables Eve trace content capture and is not a model or auth setting)                                                                                                     |

Secrets are decoded as `Redacted` values through owner Schemas. The state,
replay prefix, store prefix, routing tokens, and config namespace intentionally
do not read the removed legacy Sendblue path. Git history and retained rollout
evidence are the only legacy rollback sources.

The replay URL/token names are created by the existing Vercel Marketplace
Upstash resource connected with the exact `BUNDJIL_CHANNEL_REPLAY_` prefix.
They are provider-owned bindings, not values copied from `vercel env pull`;
sensitive Vercel variables are non-readable after creation and must never be
rebound from their placeholder export.

Neither clean provider route is current Production behavior merely because it
exists in source or builds. A provider-selection and Production-promotion SPEC
must be accepted before deployment, environment binding, webhook cutover, or
legacy deployment retirement.

## Public commands

Run from the repository root:

```bash
bun run --filter @bundjil/agent dev:no-ui
bun run --filter @bundjil/agent check-types
bun run --filter @bundjil/agent test
bun run --filter @bundjil/agent build
bun run --filter @bundjil/agent preflight:production
```

`preflight:production` is a deliberately explicit read-only gate command. It
emits one bounded receipt plus an integrity-checked sanitized detail artifact;
it does not grant deployment authority or establish current provider state.
`test` builds both the ordinary local Nitro output and the Vercel Build Output
before running fixtures; generated artifacts remain ignored local preflight.

## Documentation routes

- Durable app/runtime and Channel call graphs:

# @bundjil/codex

Effect contracts and runtime services for Bundjil Codex profiles and the
private provider path.

## Purpose and public boundary

The package owns Codex identity, profile, token, request, stream, persistence,
and safe-error Schemas; named services and Layers for encrypted profile storage,
credential validity and refresh, direct Responses proof, request/stream mapping,
and the private proxy contract. Raw HTTP services and byte streams remain inside
the package's provider/runtime composition. Tests inject a standard Effect HTTP
client only through the explicit `testing` subpath. The package also exports
explicit `runtime`, `local`, `testing`, and `filesystem-store` subpaths.
Proof and live streaming share one bounded SSE framing owner and require a
decoded `response.completed` event before reporting clean completion. The
framer preserves exact LF, CRLF and CR wire bytes across chunk boundaries,
bounds line fragments and event fields, and counts every field plus the blank
terminator toward the aggregate ceiling. A closed shared event state machine
validates recognized data and terminal events, requires exact zero-based
sequence progression, and rejects failed, incomplete, malformed, duplicate,
regressing, skipped and post-terminal streams. It strips a UTF-8 BOM only at
stream start and preserves colonless `data` as an empty event field. Arbitrary
protocol JSON is opaque, encoding-stable and limited to 32 nested containers
before event selection or object-root tool mapping. Decoding and encoding
detach and deeply freeze canonical ordinary JSON rather than retaining
caller-owned mutable arrays, objects, accessors, or proxies. Schema guards and
type-side constructors accept only deeply frozen containers produced by the
package transform, tracked through private weak identity. Frozen caller-owned
objects and proxies therefore cannot bypass detachment, while ordinary decode
still detaches them into stable encodable data. The
credential-bearing
client accepts only the owned ChatGPT Responses endpoint; access-token and
account-ID values remain distinctly branded inside redaction, while header
values are bounded and defensively constructed through a fixed secret-negative
error path. The private client explicitly requests SSE and sends the fixed
Codex compatibility headers required by the checked reference clients; callers
cannot override those headers. A successful response with no `Content-Type`
header is treated as the requested SSE type, matching the checked subscription
client behaviour. An explicit non-SSE media type is still rejected before body
ownership.
Raw provider headers and transport services remain private; successful metadata
uses the closed `text/event-stream` literal.

The expected private-proxy token is a stable Layer dependency, never an
operation-input field. Responses transport policy is decoded with Effect
Config. Defaults are 30 seconds for response headers, 30 seconds between
non-empty body chunks, 32 MiB cumulative body bytes, and 100,000 SSE events.
Zero-length transport chunks do not count as progress. Deployments may override
the limits with `BUNDJIL_CODEX_RESPONSES_HEADER_TIMEOUT_MILLIS`,
`BUNDJIL_CODEX_RESPONSES_STREAM_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MILLIS`,
`BUNDJIL_CODEX_RESPONSES_MAXIMUM_BODY_BYTES`, and
`BUNDJIL_CODEX_RESPONSES_MAXIMUM_EVENTS`. Values must be positive integers.
Proof responses remain scoped through complete validation and consumption.
Streaming responses transfer a dedicated request scope to the returned body;
early status/media rejection aborts immediately without reading body bytes.
After accepted status, media type and metadata are validated, an Effect-clock
ownership watchdog closes that scope at the stream-idle deadline unless body
subscription claims it. It does not run during the independent header timeout.
The claim is exactly once: only the winning subscriber receives the one-shot
upstream body; a subscriber after expiry or after another subscriber receives a
fixed typed stream error without touching the body. Scope closure signals the
watchdog, so normal completion, failure, cancellation and interruption leave no
detached work.

Apps own HTTP servers, deployment configuration, model selection, and provider
operations. `@bundjil/store` owns provider-neutral persistence primitives. The
exact exports, Schemas, and runtime graph are owned by code and package exports;
durable design rules are in
[`docs/architecture/`](../../docs/architecture/README.md).

The package preserves trusted-local and hosted compositions as explicit code
boundaries. Their commands do not establish current provider state or authorize
an external operation.

## Public commands

Run from the repository root:

```bash

bun run --filter @bundjil/codex test
bun run --filter @bundjil/codex build
```

The package also exposes intentionally explicit local import, subscription
login, and proof commands through `package.json`. They require authorized,
